benefits: Shows at a glance how much cheaper simple interest is than compound over long periods.
Answers everyday questions - loan cost, deposit growth - in seconds.
The side-by-side toggle teaches the compounding lesson better than any textbook paragraph.

faqs.a: Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal: I = P x r x t. Compound interest is calculated on principal plus accumulated interest: A = P x (1 + r)^t. Compounding makes money grow faster - and makes debt grow faster too.
faqs.q: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?

faqs.a: Almost always compound, and usually daily or monthly rather than yearly. Banks compound your savings (good for you) and credit cards compound your debt (bad for you). The toggle in this calculator shows the gap for your exact numbers.
faqs.q: Do banks use simple or compound interest?

faqs.a: Rearrange the simple-interest formula: t = I / (P x r). For $500 of interest on $10,000 at 5%: t = 500 / (10,000 x 0.05) = 1 year. With compounding you would solve t = ln(A/P) / ln(1 + r).
faqs.q: How do I find the time needed?

faqs.a: Rearrange: r = I / (P x t). If $10,000 earned $1,800 over 3 years with simple interest, r = 1,800 / (10,000 x 3) = 0.06 = 6%.
faqs.q: How do I find the interest rate?

faqs.a: Yes. Divide the annual rate by 12 and use months as the time unit, or divide by 365 for days. A 6% annual rate is 0.5% per month. The formula works with any consistent time unit.
faqs.q: Can I use months instead of years?

faqs.a: It is interest on interest - the reason savings accelerate and debts snowball. Over 30 years at 7%, $10,000 compounded yearly becomes $76,123, while simple interest only reaches $31,000. Time is the fuel.
faqs.q: Why is compounding called the eighth wonder of the world?

simple-interest-calculator.formula:
Simple: Interest = P x r x t. Total = P x (1 + r x t).
Compound (yearly): Total = P x (1 + r)^t. Interest = Total - P.
P = principal, r = annual rate as a decimal, t = years.
howTo: Choose Simple or Compound with the toggle.
Enter the principal - the starting amount of money.
Enter the annual interest rate as a percentage.
Enter the time in years (fractions like 2.5 are fine).
Compare the interest earned and the total for both modes.
keyFacts: Simple interest: I = P x r x t - interest is charged only on the original principal.
Compound interest: A = P x (1 + r)^t - interest earns interest on itself.
The gap between the two grows explosively with time and with the rate.
Short-term loans and some bonds use simple interest; savings accounts and credit cards compound.
Always confirm whether a quoted rate compounds, and how often.

simple-interest-calculator.quickAnswer: Simple interest is calculated only on the original amount: $10,000 at 6% for 3 years earns 10,000 x 0.06 x 3 = $1,800, for a total of $11,800. Compound interest earns interest on the interest: $10,000 x (1.06)^3 = $11,910.16, so $1,910.16 of interest. The difference looks small over 3 years, but over 30 years at 7%, compounding turns $10,000 into $76,123 while simple interest only reaches $31,000.

simple-interest-calculator.workedExample:
$10,000 principal, 6% annual, 3 years:
Simple:
1. Interest = 10,000 x 0.06 x 3 = $1,800.
2. Total = 10,000 + 1,800 = $11,800.
Compound (yearly):
1. Total = 10,000 x (1.06)^3 = 10,000 x 1.191016 = $11,910.16.
2. Interest = 11,910.16 - 10,000 = $1,910.16.
Compounding earned an extra $110.16 over 3 years.
